lecture_context.lecture_title: Lecture 3: Full Cycle of a Deep Learning Project

unit.name: Face-recognition system setup and Siamese-network architecture
unit.description: Introduces the concrete face-recognition security application and the two-image Siamese-network formulation used throughout the lecture.
unit.summary: A common face-recognition architecture is a Siamese network that takes two pictures and predicts whether they show the same person [ts=590s]. Registration photos are compared against a live or recent photo when someone approaches or swipes a card, avoiding the need to retrain a classifier for every home or office [ts=637s]. The instructor then turns the example into a startup design scenario: if internet data cannot be downloaded, the team must decide how to collect face data and how soon to start training [ts=681s]. Student suggestions include video-streaming sources, opt-in camera collection, friends or users, and institutional email outreach, but the instructor leaves the problem open to emphasize real resource constraints [ts=842s].

key_points.text: A Siamese face-recognition network takes two pictures as input and predicts same person versus different person.
Registration images allow a deployed system to compare an arriving person with authorized identities without retraining per site.
The data-collection problem is constrained by law, startup resources, and time, not only by model architecture.
Candidate data sources discussed include opt-in camera collection, friends, user submissions, video calls, and institutional outreach.
